variables.name: issued_type
variables.description: The token type written into the payload when the token was created (NewPayload's tokenType, stored as payload.Type). Opaque identity, taken from the single NewPayload call earlier in the test.

variables.name: expected_type
variables.description: The token type the verifier demands (VerifyToken's tokenType, passed unchanged to Payload.Valid). Same opaque value at both boundaries.

variables.name: expected_is_access
variables.description: The expected type is TokenTypeAccessToken (literal 1).

variables.name: expected_is_refresh
variables.description: The expected type is TokenTypeRefreshToken (literal 2).

variables.name: token_expired
variables.description: The token was created with a non-positive duration, so its ExpiredAt is in the past.

variables.name: token_authentic
variables.description: The token string decrypts/parses with the maker's key and an accepted algorithm (false for an alg=none JWT).

variables.name: rng_fails
variables.description: uuid.NewRandom fails (never in tests).

variables.name: payload_valid
variables.description: Payload.Valid returned nil (type matches and not expired).

variables.name: verify_ok
variables.description: VerifyToken returned a payload and no error.

variables.name: has_metadata
variables.description: The gRPC context carries incoming metadata.

variables.name: has_auth_header
variables.description: An authorization header is present (HTTP header or gRPC metadata key).

variables.name: header_has_two_fields
variables.description: The authorization header splits into at least two whitespace-separated fields.

variables.name: scheme_is_bearer
variables.description: The first header field, lower-cased, is 'bearer'.

variables.name: role_permitted
variables.description: The payload role is in accessibleRoles (hasPermission's result).

variables.name: authz_ok
variables.description: authorizeUser returned a payload (no error) in the current UpdateUser call.

variables.name: has_violations
variables.description: validateUpdateUserRequest reports field violations (e.g. invalid email).

variables.name: caller_is_banker
variables.description: The authenticated role is util.BankerRole.

variables.name: caller_is_target
variables.description: The authenticated username equals the username being updated.

variables.name: password_given
variables.description: The update request sets a new password.

variables.name: db_update_failed
variables.description: store.UpdateUser returns an error.

variables.name: db_not_found
variables.description: The store error is db.ErrRecordNotFound.

false_branch.effect: payload decoded, validated against expected type

true_branch.effect: jwt library rejects (expiry checked by the library, before Valid)
invalid access token (expired, undecryptable, or not an access token)

transitions.when: has_metadata && has_auth_header && header_has_two_fields && scheme_is_bearer && verify_ok && role_permitted

rules.name: A token is only accepted as the type it was issued as
consequences: Payload.Valid returns ErrInvalidToken before checking expiry
VerifyToken (PASETO and JWT) returns that error and no payload
every caller that verifies fails: gRPC authorizeUser -> UpdateUser Unauthenticated; HTTP authMiddleware -> 401 abort

rules.name: An expired token of the right type is rejected (JWT: by the library at parse time; PASETO: by Valid)
Request gates (gRPC authorizeUser, HTTP authMiddleware) demand an ACCESS token
consequences: VerifyToken is called with expected_type = TokenTypeAccessToken (literal 1)
a refresh token presented as bearer fails r_type_match

rules.name: Renewing requires a REFRESH token; login issues one of each
consequences: renewAccessToken verifies req.RefreshToken with TokenTypeRefreshToken, so an access token is rejected with 401
renewAccessToken, loginUser and gapi LoginUser create access tokens with TokenTypeAccessToken and refresh tokens with TokenTypeRefreshToken

unknowns.what: Flow of the type through the token string
unknowns.why: issued_type is bound to NewPayload's argument with execution scope and compared by identity with Valid's argument; the genome cannot state that the decrypted payload.Type IS the value encoded at creation (no flow, only equality), and with two tokens created in one execution (login issues access + refresh, renew issues a new access token) the execution-scoped identity is no longer unique, so it would be unknown.

unknowns.what: Which Maker implementation a server uses
unknowns.why: Procedures call PasetoMaker.VerifyToken directly because that is what executed; interface dispatch (JWT vs PASETO maker behind token.Maker) is not expressible.

unknowns.what: loginUser, renewAccessToken, gapi LoginUser, gapi CreateUser sites
unknowns.why: Not evaluated by any shown or withheld test; not modeled beyond rule r_refresh_gate. renewAccessToken's refresh-typed VerifyToken and session checks would need store/session variables and a relation between the session's stored refresh token and the request token.
It iterates over accessibleRoles; iteration/membership is not available, so role_permitted is an input bound to hasPermission's bool result.
For JWT, expiry is enforced inside jwt.ParseWithClaims (library), so Valid's expiry branch is effectively unreachable for JWT; modeled by making the parse decision depend on token_expired.
TokenTypeAccessToken/RefreshToken are untyped constants converted to TokenType (byte); the literal bindings assume the observed value is uint8 1/2.
